# Create static LDAP roles

Configure static roles to map names in Vault to LDAP entries and use the
rotation settings to manage credentials automatically with the role.

<Tip title="Assumptions">

- You have [set up an `ldap` plugin](/vault/docs/secrets/ldap/setup). 
- You have permission to update roles in Vault.
- You have permission to make `POST` calls to the `ldap` plugin.

</Tip>

For self-managed roles, use Vault Enterprise 2.2.0 or later and set
`self_managed=true` when you first configure the mount with the CLI or API.
You cannot change this setting after configuration, and the GUI configuration
form does not include it. Do not set `bindpass` on a self-managed mount.
For example:

```shell-session
$ vault secrets enable -path=self-managed-ldap ldap
$ vault write self-managed-ldap/config \
    url="ldaps://ldap.example.com" \
    schema="openldap" \
    self_managed=true
```

<Tabs>

<Tab heading="CLI" group="cli">

1. Create a configuration file, `ldap-role.json`, with your role settings:

   @include 'ldap/example-config/static-role/basic.mdx'

   For a self-managed mount, also include the account's current `password`.

1. Save the new role:

   @include 'ldap/create-static-role/cli.mdx'

   For example, to create a self-managed role without a configuration file:

   ```shell-session
   $ vault write self-managed-ldap/static-role/billing-svc \
       dn="cn=billing-svc,ou=services,dc=example,dc=com" \
       username="billing-svc" \
       password="<current-password>" \
       rotation_period=0
   ```

1. Confirm the role settings by requesting credentials from the plugin:

   @include 'ldap/get-role-creds/cli.mdx'

</Tab>

<Tab heading="API" group="api">

1. Create a configuration file, `ldap-role.json`, with your role settings:

   @include 'ldap/example-config/static-role/basic.mdx'

   For a self-managed mount, also include the account's current `password`.

1. Save the new role:

   @include 'ldap/create-static-role/api.mdx'

1. Confirm the role settings by requesting credentials from the plugin:

   @include 'ldap/get-role-creds/api.mdx'

</Tab>

<Tab heading="GUI" group="gui">

The GUI reads the `self_managed` setting from the mount configuration and shows
the matching form. Follow the section for your mount type.

Your policy must grant the following capabilities:

| GUI action | Path | Capability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Detect the mount type | `<mount>/config` | `read` |
| Show **Create role** and create the role | `<mount>/static-role/<name>` | `create` |
| View the role | `<mount>/static-role/<name>` | `read` |
| Show the **Password** row and **Get credentials** | `<mount>/static-cred/<name>` | `read` |

For example:

```hcl
path "<mount>/config"        { capabilities = ["read"] }
path "<mount>/static-role/*" { capabilities = ["create", "read", "list"] }
path "<mount>/static-cred/*" { capabilities = ["read"] }
```

The form covers the role name, distinguished name, username, password, and
rotation period. To set other parameters, such as `password_policy` or
`rotation_schedule`, use the CLI or API.

### Root-managed mount

1. Open the Vault GUI, go to **Secrets engines**, and select your root-managed
   LDAP mount.

1. Open the **Roles** tab and click **Create role**.

1. For **Role type**, select **Static role**.

1. Enter a **Role name**, such as `billing-svc`.

1. Enter the **Username** of the existing LDAP entry.

1. Optionally, enter the **Distinguished name** of the entry, such as:

   `cn=billing-svc,ou=services,dc=example,dc=com`

1. Optionally, enter the account's current **Password**. Vault returns it as the
   starting password until the first rotation.

1. Set **Rotation period** to the interval between automatic password
   rotations. Leave it empty or set it to `0` to disable automatic rotation.

1. Click **Create role**. Vault creates the role and opens its details page.

### Self-managed mount

1. Open the Vault GUI, go to **Secrets engines**, and select your self-managed
   LDAP mount.

1. Open the **Roles** tab and click **Create role**. The **Create static role**
   form opens without role type options, because self-managed mounts support
   only static roles.

1. Enter a **Role name**, such as `billing-svc`.

1. Enter the **Distinguished name** of the existing LDAP entry, such as:

   `cn=billing-svc,ou=services,dc=example,dc=com`

   You cannot change it after you create the role.

1. Enter the **Username** of the entry.

1. Enter the account's current LDAP **Password**. Vault uses it to manage future
   rotations.

1. Set **Rotation period** to the interval between automatic password
   rotations. Leave it empty or set it to `0` to disable automatic rotation.

1. Click **Create role**. Vault creates the role and opens its details page.

### View the role credentials

1. On the role's details page, click the eye icon in the **Password** row to
   show the password, or use the copy icon to copy it.

1. Click **Get credentials** to open the credentials page, which shows:

   | Field | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | Last Vault rotation | When Vault last rotated the password, or `Never` if it has not. |
   | Password | The current password, masked by default. |
   | Username | The LDAP username. |
   | Rotation period | The configured period. `0` means automatic rotation is off. |
   | Time remaining | The time until the next automatic rotation. |

<Note>

Vault Enterprise 2.2.0 and 2.2.1 display a placeholder date in the year 0001
instead of `Never` for roles that Vault has not rotated.

</Note>

### Restricted permissions

If your policy does not grant `read` on `<mount>/config`, the GUI cannot detect
the mount type. The create page then shows **Unable to determine LDAP
configuration mode** and the root-managed form. On a self-managed mount, Vault
rejects a role without a distinguished name or password, and the form shows
the error. Add the missing value and click **Create role** again. To get the
self-managed form, grant `read` on `<mount>/config`.

</Tab>
